security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown inline code or fenced examples, not Ruby shell backtick execution or malicious networking. The main residual concern is the recommendation to globally install an unpinned npm package with @latest.

State that browser navigation, form submission, and package commands should run only after user approval and only against authorized sites.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Testing with Playwright CLI
content.value_statement: Manual page inspection slows web testing and ScreenCI script creation. This skill guides Playwright CLI browser sessions, snapshots, selectors, and repeatable interaction checks.
actual_capabilities: Open browser sessions and navigate to target pages with Playwright CLI.
Capture full-page or element snapshots for inspection and comparison.
Interact with page elements using refs, CSS selectors, and Playwright locators.
Click, type, fill, select, hover, check, uncheck, and press keys.
Evaluate simple page or element JavaScript for inspection tasks.
Manage named browser sessions and close active browser instances.
limitations: Requires Playwright CLI or a compatible local package to be available.
Only works against pages reachable from the execution environment.
Browser commands can submit forms or change page state if approved.
Snapshots describe current page state but do not replace full test assertions.

use_cases.title: Inspect a User Flow
use_cases.description: Navigate a live page, capture snapshots, and identify stable selectors before writing automated tests.

use_cases.title: Debug Frontend Behavior
use_cases.description: Run focused browser interactions and inspect page output while diagnosing UI or selector issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare ScreenCI Scripts
use_cases.description: Discover consent steps, hidden setup actions, and reliable locators for a ScreenCI recording workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright CLI to open the target page, take a snapshot, and summarize the visible elements and likely next action.

prompt_templates.title: Find Stable Selectors
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this page with Playwright CLI and recommend stable refs, roles, or test IDs for the main interaction flow.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Page States
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture a before snapshot, perform the approved interaction, capture an after snapshot, and explain what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a ScreenCI Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore the flow with Playwright CLI, identify cookie consent setup, and outline the ScreenCI steps with stable locators.

output_examples.input: Inspect the home page and find the search interaction.
output_examples.output: The page exposes a search box with a stable role locator. The next safe action is to type the approved query and submit.

output_examples.input: Compare the page before and after clicking the submit button.
output_examples.output: The after snapshot shows a confirmation message and disabled submit button. No unexpected navigation was observed.

output_examples.input: Prepare a ScreenCI flow for a page with a cookie banner.
output_examples.output: Use a hidden setup step to accept the banner, then record only the visible product interaction steps.

best_practices: Run commands only against sites and environments you are authorized to test.
Prefer stable roles, test IDs, and refs over brittle visual selectors.
Review snapshots before submitting forms or performing state-changing actions.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass authentication, consent, or access controls.
Do not submit real credentials or production data during exploratory runs.
Do not install global packages without version pinning and user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill run a real browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides Playwright CLI commands that open and control browser sessions.

faq.question: Can it create Playwright tests automatically?
faq.answer: It helps inspect flows and selectors, but generated tests still need review and assertions.

faq.question: Does it support ScreenCI workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for discovering setup actions and selectors before writing ScreenCI scripts.

faq.question: Can it interact with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Only if the execution environment has authorized access and the user approves the actions.

faq.question: Will it install Playwright CLI?
faq.answer: It can suggest installation steps, but installation should be pinned and explicitly approved.

faq.question: Are snapshots the same as screenshots?
faq.answer: No. Snapshots describe page structure and element refs for automation, not visual image output.
